## 7. Theoretically Related Variables

> **Correspondence to manuscript:** 
>
> Correlation estimates in this section reproduce the associations between PHQ-8 scores and theoretically related constructs reported in Table 8 of the manuscript.

Correlations were computed between PHQ-8 mean scores and a set of theoretically related constructs (depressive symptoms, anxiety, perceived stress, brooding rumination, self-deprecation, positive self-esteem, and quality of life). Correlations were estimated for the total sample, by sex, and separately within Filipino American and European American subgroups using pairwise-complete observations. These analyses were conducted to evaluate convergent and discriminant validity of the PHQ-8 across groups.

::: callout-note
#### Syntax scaffolding: Correlational validity with related constructs

- **Goal.** This chunk reproduces the correlations between PHQ-8 scores and theoretically related constructs for the total sample and the sex- and ethnicity-based subgroups reported in Table 8.

  **Scales and variables.**

  - `phq_mean` is the mean PHQ-8 score created earlier in the workflow.

  - The theoretically related variables are `cesd_mean`, `gad_mean`, `stress_mean`, `brood_mean`, `selfdep_mean`, `posesteem_mean`, and `qol`, representing depressive symptoms, anxiety, perceived stress, brooding rumination, self-deprecation, positive esteem, and quality of life, respectively.

  **Correlation and confidence-interval estimation.**

  The helper function `compute_r_ci()` calculates the Pearson correlation between `phq_mean` and each related variable. For each correlation, the function:

  - retains complete observations for the specific pair of variables,

  - calculates the Pearson correlation,

  - generates 5,000 nonparametric bootstrap samples,

  - derives a 95% percentile bootstrap confidence interval, and

  - formats the estimate and confidence limits without leading zeros.

  Cases with insufficient observations or no variation in either variable are returned as missing.

  **Subgroup organization.**

  The helper function `make_corr_column()` applies `compute_r_ci()` to every theoretically related variable. Correlations are calculated for:

  - the total sample,

  - men and women in the total sample,

  - Filipino Americans overall, Filipino American men, and Filipino American women, and

  - European Americans overall, European American men, and European American women.

  `set.seed(2026)` is used before estimation so that the bootstrap confidence intervals are reproducible across renders.

  **Tabling.**

  The formatted correlation strings are assembled into a single data frame and passed to `gt::gt()`. The resulting table contains one row for each theoretically related construct and separate columns for the total sample and each subgroup. `gt` functions are used to apply readable column labels, grouped subgroup headings, alignment, and the table note.

  **Software dependencies.**

  - Base R: correlation estimation, resampling, subsetting, indexing, and formatting.

  - `gt`: construction and formatting of the final Table 8 output.
:::

```{r}
#| label: phq-related-correlations-table
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# PHQ-8 vs. theoretically related constructs (Table 8)
# Correlations with bootstrap 95% CIs
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

related_vars <- c(
  "cesd_mean",
  "gad_mean",
  "stress_mean",
  "brood_mean",
  "selfdep_mean",
  "posesteem_mean",
  "qol"
)

related_labels <- c(
  "CES-D-10",
  "Anxiety",
  "Perceived stress",
  "Brooding rumination",
  "Self-deprecation",
  "Positive esteem",
  "Quality of life"
)

# APA-style number formatting: .44 instead of 0.44
apa_r <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  out <- sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x)
  out <- sub("^0\\.", ".", out)
  out <- sub("^-0\\.", "-.", out)
  out
}

# Helper: bootstrap correlation CI for phq_mean with a given variable
compute_r_ci <- function(data, y_var, x_var = "phq_mean", R = 5000, conf = .95) {
  
  # Keep only the two variables needed for this correlation
  d <- data[, c(x_var, y_var)]
  
  # Use complete cases for this specific pair of variables
  d <- d[complete.cases(d), ]
  
  # Store pairwise n
  n <- nrow(d)
  
  # Return missing if there are too few cases or no variation
  if (
    n < 4 ||
    sd(d[[x_var]], na.rm = TRUE) == 0 ||
    sd(d[[y_var]], na.rm = TRUE) == 0
  ) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }
  
  # Observed Pearson correlation
  r_obs <- cor(d[[x_var]], d[[y_var]])
  
  # Bootstrap correlations
  boot_rs <- replicate(R, {
    idx <- sample.int(n, size = n, replace = TRUE)
    
    x_boot <- d[[x_var]][idx]
    y_boot <- d[[y_var]][idx]
    
    # Some bootstrap samples may have zero variance; suppress warning and return NA
    suppressWarnings(cor(x_boot, y_boot))
  })
  
  # Remove failed bootstrap samples
  boot_rs <- boot_rs[!is.na(boot_rs)]
  
  # Percentile bootstrap CI
  alpha <- 1 - conf
  ci <- quantile(
    boot_rs,
    probs = c(alpha / 2, 1 - alpha / 2),
    na.rm = TRUE,
    names = FALSE
  )
  
  # Format as r [LL, UL]
  paste0(
    apa_r(r_obs),
    " [",
    apa_r(ci[1]),
    ", ",
    apa_r(ci[2]),
    "]"
  )
}

# Helper: apply the correlation + CI function to all related variables
make_corr_column <- function(data) {
  sapply(
    related_vars,
    function(v) compute_r_ci(data, v, R = 5000),
    USE.NAMES = FALSE
  )
}

# Set seed once so the bootstrap CIs are reproducible
set.seed(2026)

# Construct correlation table across total / sex / ethnicity cells
corr_df <- data.frame(
  Related_Variable = related_labels,
  Total_Both  = make_corr_column(phq_total),
  Total_Men   = make_corr_column(subset(phq_total, female == 0)),
  Total_Women = make_corr_column(subset(phq_total, female == 1)),
  Fil_Total   = make_corr_column(subset(phq_total, filipino == 1)),
  Fil_Men     = make_corr_column(subset(phq_total, filipino == 1 & female == 0)),
  Fil_Women   = make_corr_column(subset(phq_total, filipino == 1 & female == 1)),
  Eur_Total   = make_corr_column(subset(phq_total, filipino == 0)),
  Eur_Men     = make_corr_column(subset(phq_total, filipino == 0 & female == 0)),
  Eur_Women   = make_corr_column(subset(phq_total, filipino == 0 & female == 1)),
  check.names = FALSE
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Format correlation table with gt
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

gt_phq_corr <- corr_df %>%
  gt::gt() %>%
  gt::cols_label(
    Related_Variable = "Related Variable",
    Total_Both       = "Total Sample\nBoth",
    Total_Men        = "Total Sample\nMen",
    Total_Women      = "Total Sample\nWomen",
    Fil_Total        = "Filipino Americans\nTotal",
    Fil_Men          = "Filipino Americans\nMen",
    Fil_Women        = "Filipino Americans\nWomen",
    Eur_Total        = "European Americans\nTotal",
    Eur_Men          = "European Americans\nMen",
    Eur_Women        = "European Americans\nWomen"
  ) %>%
  gt::cols_align(
    align   = "left",
    columns = Related_Variable
  ) %>%
  gt::cols_align(
    align   = "center",
    columns = -Related_Variable
  ) %>%
  gt::tab_header(
    title = "Correlations of PHQ-8 with Theoretically Related Constructs"
  ) %>%
  gt::tab_source_note(
    source_note = "Note. Cells report Pearson correlations with 95% percentile bootstrap confidence intervals in brackets, based on 5,000 resamples. Correlations use pairwise complete observations; therefore, sample sizes may vary across constructs and subgroups."
  )
```
